Score DV-L3-01: RAGBot chained prompt injection → disclosure of KB docs (admin credentials, SSN).

CVSS: AV — documented default deployment. Ports bind 127.0.0.1 (npm) but Docker publishes on 127.0.0.1; to attack remotely operator must expose. Documented default is loopback, so attacker needs local/adjacent... The entry point is "chat message to port 7005, no auth." Documented default deployment binds loopback. AV: L (local access or user on that system) — but attacker is the party sending the chat message; if loopback, local. Score L? The briefing says score as documented default deployment. Default binds 127.0.0.1 → AV:L. PR:N (no auth), UI:N, AC:L, AT:N. VC:H (admin password + SSN disclosed — high-value info), VI:N, VA:N. Subsequent: none beyond agent. SC:N SI:N SA:N.

Actually attacker doesn't already own the asset (the KB secrets).

AIVSS:
- LC: attack is via user message directly to agent chat → D (direct). Though the challenge is "indirect via retrieved content", the actual code path: user message drives dataExfiltration reply; the KB is static, no ingestion path ("the demo delivers the poisoned document inside the user message"). So attacker-supplied NL reaches the disclosure path directly → D.
- CP: stateless per request; memoryStore only for MemoryBot; no cross-session persistence → N.
- AP: confined to RAGBot component → N.
- RH: no evaluator on the path; agent can reach... The challenge has successCriteria pattern in challenges/index.js — but is that in the agent's reach? The success criteria is a grading pattern for the CTF; agent can't tamper with it. Reachable proxy? The scoring path (trackCategorySuccessful) runs in the same process — agent could potentially... but no tool on the documented path reaches it. No verified episodes. Set reachable_proxy false, isolation not verified → X? Rubric: N requires unreachable AND verified test; X otherwise unless reachable=true with 0 episodes → P. Is there a proxy/evaluator reachable on the path? trackCategorySuccessful is in the same process; RAGBot has submit_to_index HTTP call, but path doesn't invoke tools. The agent could exfiltrate... hmm. I'd say reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified null → X. Actually classify_rh: verified_episodes 0 (no episodes), reachable false, isolation not verified → X. Set verified_episodes 0, reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified null → RH=X.
- ES: path's reachable extension surface — RAGBot's submit_to_index makes real HTTP GET with URL from message (external write), but named_in_documented_path false and path doesn't reach it. Reachable? The agent declares submit_to_index tool. But the assessed path (chat → exfil reply) has no tool. ES: N? Extensions not on the path → N ("No security-relevant dynamic extension on the path"). Actually the chat path is entirely scripted. ES=N.

Automatable: Yes — simple HTTP request, scripted response; no human needed.
Technical impact: Partial (disclosure of specific docs, no code exec).

Applicability: model_directed_goal_pursuit — LLM mode optional; default is simulated scripted replies. As implemented: false, false. As modeled (documentation describes agent with LLM optional): the documented agent is a persona with retrieval; docs describe LLM mode... "as documentation describes it" — the agent as documented is an AI assistant that retrieves docs and answers, with optional LLM mode. I'd say modeled: model_directed_goal_pursuit true (LLM mode documented as the real exploitation path), selects_or_sequences_actions false (no tools passed to model). Confidence medium/low.

Evidence lists.

CVSS vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

AV debate: could argue N because no auth and entry is network; but documented default binds loopback → Adjacent? Loopback isn't shared network. L is right per rubric ("local session"). Attacker needs local access to the machine. AV:L.

Confidence keys: LC high, CP high, AP high, RH low, ES medium, CVSS medium.

rh_facts: reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified null, verified_episodes 0, episodes_reviewed 0, locus null (X letter, locus not required).
